chunks: What was narrated by Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from some of our companions, who said:
He said to me: “The salat of the day is sixteen rakʿahs. Pray it at whichever part of the day you wish: if you wish, at its beginning; if you wish, in its middle; and if you wish, at its end.”

key_terms.آخِرِهِ: its end, meaning the latter part of the day
key_terms.أَوَّلِهِ: its beginning, meaning the beginning of the day
key_terms.النَّهَارِ: the daytime, indicating the period in which these prayers are performed
key_terms.سِتَّ عَشْرَةَ: sixteen, the total number of rakʿahs mentioned
key_terms.صَلَاةُ: salat (prayer), referring here to the daytime prayer units
key_terms.صَلِّهَا: perform it, meaning to offer these prayers
key_terms.وَسَطِهِ: its middle, meaning the middle of the day

ai.seo_question: When can the sixteen rakʿahs of the daytime salat be performed?
ai.summary: This hadith states the prescribed number of daytime supererogatory salat as sixteen rakʿahs and indicates flexibility in performing them during the day. It conveys a jurisprudential ruling concerning the timing and allowance of these recommended prayers.
